learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how British colonialism completely rewired India's economy, cities, and industries, leaving a lasting impact on our modern structure!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Unlike previous rulers who settled and assimilated, the British integrated India into global capitalism solely to extract wealth for the benefit of Britain.
As Britain industrialized, they flooded India with cheap machine-made goods. This destroyed India's world-famous traditional handloom and craft industries, forcing artisans back into agriculture.
The British set up industries like Tea Plantations in Assam. However, they used cruel laws to trap laborers (who lived in miserable conditions) to maximize profits.
Old coastal cities like Surat declined, while British port cities like Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras grew massively to facilitate the export of raw materials.

fun_activity.title: ☕ The Tea Story
fun_activity.instructions: Next time you drink tea, remember its colonial roots. Research how the British aggressively promoted tea-drinking in India by giving out free samples at railway stations in the early 1900s to create a domestic market!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate between Western industrialization (which created jobs) and Indian colonial industrialization (which caused deindustrialisation and loss of livelihoods).
📌 Highlight the paradox of the Tea Plantations: modern capitalist enterprise run using forced, slave-like labor.
📌 Mention how the British introduced railways not for Indian development, but to easily transport resources and troops.
quick_recap: ⭐ Structural change refers to fundamental shifts in the economy, institutions, and living patterns.
⭐ Capitalism drove the British colonial enterprise, focusing entirely on profit maximization.
⭐ The rise of metropolitan port cities was a direct result of colonial trade requirements.
